example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, a two-member LLC, closing the year ended 31 December 2025. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.2024-schedule-k1s.pdf: the name of the user's own file of last year's Schedule K-1s

messages.text: Can you close our books for 2025?
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload the data?
Which company? For a group, which entities?
When does your fiscal year end?
Is the business a corporation, partnership, LLC, sole proprietor or nonprofit?
For a partnership or LLC: how do the members share profit, and do you keep capital for each member?
Which framework: US GAAP, IFRS or other?
Is this the final trial balance, with all adjusting entries posted?
Does your accounting system close the year by itself when you move to the new year?
Do you close straight to retained earnings, or through an Income Summary account?
Do you report on a cash or an accrual basis?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading. It is an LLC. Lena Hart gets 60% and Omar Vance 40%, with capital kept for each. US GAAP, accrual. We have no Income Summary account. All adjustments are in. I think QuickBooks closes the year. The audit is not done. Last year's K-1s are attached.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I close **FY2025**, the year ended **31 December 2025**, for **Northbrook Trading**, an LLC with capital for each member. I use the **two-step** method, straight to capital, because you have no Income Summary account. The audit is not complete, so this is a **preliminary close**. Before I propose any entry, I test whether QuickBooks already closed the year. Shall I start?
Yes, go ahead.

messages.label: Read the books in one batch
rows: 24 accounts, includes Customer Deposits as Other Income
messages.summary: 6 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: Before I go on, one account needs your answer. **Customer Deposits** has the type Other Income and a credit of $4,000. The name says money that customers paid in advance. That is a liability, not income.
messages.after: Net income agrees with the P&L at 212,900, because the P&L follows the same type. So only a check of names against types finds this. Which is right, the name or the type?

messages.text: The name. Customers paid that money in advance.
Then the trial balance is not final yet. A type correction is an adjusting entry, so I stop here. Please post this in QuickBooks, dated 31 December 2025:
messages.after: Net income then falls to **$208,900**. Tell me when it is posted, and I read everything again.

messages.text: Posted. Please run it again.

messages.label: Read the books again, and tested the closed state
rows: 1 Jan 2026, every income and expense account at 0
messages.summary: 6 reads in one batch. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: You were right. **QuickBooks already closed the year.** On 1 January 2026, every income and expense account is at 0. No closing entry exists, and Retained Earnings holds the year's $208,900.
messages.after: So I propose no entry that closes revenue or expenses. A second close would count the profit twice and overstate equity by $208,900.

messages.text: The final trial balance balances at **1,724,000** on each side. Opening capital is $350,000: $210,000 for Lena and $140,000 for Omar. That agrees with the ending capital on your 2024 K-1s.
QuickBooks moved the profit into Retained Earnings. It did not split it between the members, and it did not close their distributions. I propose two entries for that:

card.title: Proposed entries, 31 Dec 2025
head: Entry
Amount
Debit and credit
rows: Dr Retained Earnings, Cr Member Capital (Hart)
Dr Retained Earnings, Cr Member Capital (Vance)
Dr Member Capital (Hart), Cr Member Distributions (Hart)
Dr Member Capital (Vance), Cr Member Distributions (Vance)

messages.after: Each account has its own name from your chart. A person posts these entries. I do not.

messages.text: After P1 and P2, the members' capital moves by exactly the profit and the distributions:
messages.after: The post-closing trial balance balances at **591,400** on each side. It holds only permanent accounts. Assets and liabilities did not change.

messages.text: This is a preliminary close. If the audit changes any figure, I run the tests again. Your workpaper has eight sheets, with the closed-state finding in its header.
messages.after: Do you want the workpaper as an Excel file?

messages.text: Yes. And please post P1 and P2, then lock 2025 for me.
Here is **Closing_Entries_TB_FY2025_Northbrook Trading.xlsx**. I cannot post or lock anything. A person posts P1 and P2 in QuickBooks. Who locks 2025, and when?
Lena does, after the audit.
Thank you. The coverage sheet names the lock as a manual step for Lena Hart, after the audit.
messages.after: Do you want me to save your settings for next year?

messages.text: Yes, save them.

Done. I saved the entity type, the profit shares, the two-step method, that QuickBooks closes the year, the Customer Deposits exception and who locks the period. I never save balances. Next year, I test the closed state again.
